Part-Time Work Is Part of the Plan — Know the Rules Before You Go

For most international students, part-time work is not a nice-to-have — it is a core part of how they manage living costs while studying abroad. But the rules vary significantly by destination, and getting them wrong has serious consequences: working beyond your permitted hours is a visa violation that can lead to cancellation of your student visa, deportation, and a ban from re-entering the country.

Here are the confirmed 2026 work hour rules for every major study destination — with minimum wage figures so you can calculate exactly how much you can realistically earn alongside your studies.

Work Hours by Country — Confirmed 2026 Rules

🇬🇧 United Kingdom 20 hrs / week (term time)

International students at UK universities and higher education providers can work up to 20 hours per week during term time. During official university holidays — Christmas, Easter, and summer — you can work full-time with no weekly cap. Students at further education colleges studying below degree level are typically limited to 10 hours per week during term time.

Self-employment and running a business are not permitted on a UK Student Visa, regardless of hours worked.

🇦🇺 Australia 48 hrs / fortnight (term time)

Australia uses a fortnight (any consecutive 14-day period) rather than a weekly cap. During your course, you can work up to 48 hours across any 14-day window — roughly 24 hours per week. During official semester breaks and holidays, work hours are unlimited.

Master's by Research and PhD students have unlimited work rights throughout the year, including during their course. One important detail: the fortnight is measured on a rolling basis from any Monday — not fixed calendar weeks. Track your hours carefully across overlapping fortnights to avoid a breach.

🇨🇦 Canada 24 hrs / week (off-campus, term time)

As of 2026, eligible international students in Canada can work up to 24 hours per week off-campus during regular academic sessions — a reduction from the temporary 40-hour limit introduced post-pandemic. On-campus work at your own institution has no fixed hour cap, provided you remain a full-time student.

During officially scheduled breaks such as summer vacation and winter holidays, eligible students can work full-time. A valid study permit with work conditions is required — not all study permits automatically include off-campus work rights.

🇳🇿 New Zealand 25 hrs / week (updated Nov 2025)

From November 2025, Immigration New Zealand increased the part-time work allowance for eligible international students from 20 to 25 hours per week during term time — one of the most student-friendly policy updates of 2025. During scheduled course holidays and semester breaks, full-time work is permitted.

The 25-hour limit applies to students enrolled in full-time programs at degree level and above. Students in shorter or lower-level programs may face different conditions — always check your specific visa conditions.

🇺🇸 United States 20 hrs / week — on-campus only

The USA has the most restrictive student work rights of any major study destination. F-1 students are permitted to work up to 20 hours per week on-campus during term time. Off-campus work is generally not permitted — exceptions include Curricular Practical Training (CPT), which must be an integral part of your curriculum, and Optional Practical Training (OPT), which is typically authorized after graduation.

Full-time on-campus work is permitted during official university breaks. Note: 12 months of full-time CPT makes a student ineligible for OPT — a critical rule to understand before accepting any CPT arrangement.

⚠️
OPT faces major uncertainty in 2026 Following the July 2026 end of Duration of Status, the DHS regulatory agenda confirms OPT reform proposals will be published in August 2026. Students who rely on the STEM OPT pathway for their US career plan should monitor this closely and have a contingency plan ready.

🇩🇪 Germany 120 full days or 240 half days / year

Germany uses an annual model rather than a weekly cap. International students can work 120 full working days (or 240 half days) per year — which works out to roughly 20 hours per week on average, but gives you flexibility to work more intensively during holidays and less during busy academic periods.

Student jobs in Germany are known as "Nebenjobs" and are widely available in retail, hospitality, tutoring, and campus roles. Germany's minimum wage makes it a financially attractive destination for students willing to work alongside their studies.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which country allows the most work hours for international students in 2026?
Australia allows the most hours during term time — 48 hours per fortnight, equivalent to roughly 24 hours per week. Combined with Australia's high casual minimum wage of AUD $31.19 per hour, this gives international students the highest part-time earning potential of any major study destination. During official semester breaks, Australian students can work unlimited hours, making holiday periods a strong window to save significantly.
Can international students work full-time during university holidays?
Yes — in the UK, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand, international students are permitted to work full-time during officially scheduled university holiday periods, including summer, Christmas, and Easter breaks. In the USA, on-campus full-time work is permitted during official breaks, but off-campus full-time work generally remains restricted. In Germany, additional holiday work draws from your annual pool of 120 full days, so the timing of holiday work affects how much you can work throughout the rest of the year.
What happens if an international student works more than the permitted hours?
Exceeding your permitted work hours is a breach of your student visa conditions and can have serious consequences — including cancellation of your visa, removal from the country, and a ban on applying for future visas. In Australia, the Department of Home Affairs actively monitors compliance through tax records and employer reporting. In the UK, HMRC and UKVI share data to identify students working beyond their permitted hours. The rules are enforced — always track your hours carefully, particularly in Australia where the fortnightly measurement system can be easy to miscount.
Can international students work off-campus in the USA?
Generally, no. F-1 students are restricted to on-campus employment during term time — up to 20 hours per week. Off-campus work requires specific authorization through either Curricular Practical Training (CPT), which must be directly linked to your course curriculum, or Optional Practical Training (OPT), which is typically authorized after graduation. Working off-campus without this authorization is a serious visa violation. Note that 12 months of full-time CPT makes you ineligible for OPT — a critical rule to understand before accepting any CPT-based internship or placement.
